::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="t13-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>What to build</dt><dd>Seven numbers: MW of five plants and the battery's MW and MWh; each costs money every year.</dd>
<dt>Hourly operation</dt><dd>Given what is built, the solver runs the plants and the battery at least cost each hour.</dd>
<dt>Seven weeks</dt><dd>Four typical weeks and three extreme ones stand for the 52 weeks of 2025.</dd>
<dt>Storage link</dt><dd>The battery's charge carries from each calendar week to the next.</dd>
<dt>CO₂ cap</dt><dd>An extra rule; its shadow price is the cost of the last tonne cut.</dd>
<dt>Frontier</dt><dd>The cheapest plan at each CO₂ level; no plan is both cheaper and cleaner.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<style>/* lesson-local */.lx13-fallback td,.lx13-fallback th{font-size:13.5px}</style>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The capstone as a linear program</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

The model decides what to build ($K_i$) and how to run it every modelled hour $t$, at least yearly cost:

$$\min \; \sum_i f_i K_i + \sum_t w_t \big(r_\mathrm{cc}\, g_t + r_\mathrm{pk}\, q_t + V u_t\big)$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
a^{w}_t K_\mathrm{wind} + a^{s}_t K_\mathrm{solar} + 0.911\,K_\mathrm{nuc} + g_t + q_t + d_t - c_t + u_t &\ge D_t && \text{(demand)}\\
g_t \le K_\mathrm{cc}, \quad q_t \le K_\mathrm{pk}, \quad c_t + d_t &\le K_\mathrm{bp} && \text{(sizes)}\\
s_t = s_{t-1} + 0.85\,c_t - d_t, \qquad 0 \le s_t &\le K_\mathrm{be} && \text{(battery)}\\
\textstyle\sum_t w_t\,(0.329\, g_t + 0.484\, q_t) &\le \text{cap} && \text{(CO}_2\text{)}
\end{aligned}
$$

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $K_i$ | size built: wind, solar, gas CC, peaker, nuclear; battery power $K_\mathrm{bp}$ | MW |
| $K_\mathrm{be}$ | battery energy | MWh |
| $f_i$ | yearly cost of one unit built; for nuclear it also holds fuel and O&M, as its output is constant | \$ per MW-year (per MWh-year) |
| $g_t, q_t$ | output of the gas CC plant and the peaker | MW |
| $r_\mathrm{cc}, r_\mathrm{pk}$ | running cost of gas | \$/MWh |
| $c_t, d_t, s_t$ | battery charge, discharge and level | MW, MW, MWh |
| $u_t$ | demand left unserved | MW |
| $V$ | \$10,000 per unserved MWh: a weight that steers a fixed plan to keep the lights on, never counted in its cost | \$/MWh |
| $a^w_t, a^s_t$ | wind and solar output per MW built | MW per MW |
| $D_t$ | demand | MW |
| $w_t$ | hours of the year that modelled hour $t$ stands for | h |
| $0.911$ | nuclear output per MW built, the same every hour: a simplification | MW per MW |

- **Yearly cost** of a plant: [overnight capital cost]{.lx-term term="capital-cost"} × [capital recovery factor]{.lx-term term="capital-recovery-factor"} + [fixed O&M]{.lx-term term="fixed-om"} (operation and maintenance). At a 4% real (after-inflation) [cost of capital]{.lx-term term="wacc"} over 30 years, the factor is 0.05783.
- **Running cost** of gas: [heat rate]{.lx-term term="heat-rate"} × gas price + [variable O&M]{.lx-term term="variable-om"}. MMBtu is a million Btu of fuel energy.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{wind, per kW-year:}\;\; & 1{,}712 \times 0.05783 + 34.57 = \$133.6\\
\text{combined-cycle, per MWh:}\;\; & 6.226 \times \$3.85 + \$3.49 = \$27.46\\
\text{its CO}_2\text{, t per MWh:}\;\; & 6.226 \times 0.05291 = 0.329
\end{aligned}
$$

<p class="lx-hint" style="margin-top:10px">Need a refresher? Toolbox <a href="k03-discounting.html">K3</a> (discounting and the capital recovery factor).</p>

Every term is linear, so this is a [linear program]{.lx-term term="linear-program"}. Your plan fixes the $K_i$; the optimizer chooses them too, with $u_t = 0$. [M3](m03-capacity-expansion.qmd) (capacity expansion) writes the same model in code, on representative weeks checked against the full year.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Seven weeks for a year: how, and how well</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Seasons.** Each season's [representative week]{.lx-term term="representative-period"} is its medoid: the real week closest, hour by hour, to the season's other weeks. Scaled to keep the season's demand, wind and solar energy, it stands for 11 (winter), 14 (spring), 11 (summer) or 13 (fall) weeks.
- **Extremes.** Three weeks are kept as they were: the year's peak demand, the peak of demand minus wind and sun, and the least wind.
- **Storage across weeks** (after Kotzur and co-authors, 2018). Calendar week $i$ starts at level $S_i$, and its representative week $k$ adds its net change: $S_{i+1} = S_i + \Delta_k$.
- **Within each week.** Its lowest and highest swing, $\ell_k$ and $h_k$, keep $0 \le S_i + \ell_k$ and $S_i + h_k \le K_\mathrm{be}$. The year ends where it began.

The check: the optimizer's plans, rounded up to the sliders' steps, re-run hour by hour on all 8,760 hours.

| Plan | Cost, 7 weeks | Cost, full year | CO₂, 7 weeks | CO₂, full year | Unserved, full year |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Optimizer at 400 kt | $118.6M | $118.7M | 392 kt | 393 kt | 43 MWh |
| Optimizer at 200 kt | $130.5M | $132.1M | 197 kt | 215 kt | 33 MWh |
| Optimizer at 100 kt | $144.4M | $147.2M | 98 kt | 131 kt | 0 MWh |

- **Cost.** Each plan costs at most 2% more on the full year.
- **CO₂.** Deeper cuts overshoot their caps: 215 kt against 200 kt (7% over) and 131 kt against 100 kt (31% over). Seven weeks miss some still, hot evenings when gas must run.
- **Unserved energy.** Tiny: at most 43 MWh, under 0.002% of the year's demand.
- **Re-optimized on all 8,760 hours.** The cheapest 200 kt plan costs $133.2M, 3% more, and its last tonne $139 instead of $85: seven weeks underestimate the cost of deep cuts.

Planners respond with more or longer periods, extreme weeks and adequacy tests over many weather years (A5, upcoming).

</details>
</div>

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="t13-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="wind-alone" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If wind is the cheapest way to cut CO₂, the cheapest clean plan is all wind.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. On still evenings the town still needs firm plants or storage; at 100 kt the optimizer keeps 280 MW of gas and adds solar and a battery.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="spill" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The cheapest plan never spills any wind or sun.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. At a 100 kt cap the optimizer spills 9% on purpose: extra wind is cheaper than storing every last MWh.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="weeks" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Seven well-chosen weeks give exactly the same answer as the whole year.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Re-run on all 8,760 hours, the optimizer's 200 kt plan emits 215 kt and leaves 33 MWh unserved.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="t13">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="gap" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">Your plan costs $140.0M a year and emits 150 kt. The cheapest plan at 150 kt costs $134.5M. How far above the frontier are you?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">5.5%</li><li data-value="b">4.1%</li><li data-value="c">$5.5M</li><li data-value="d">150 kt</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>4.1%: 140.0 ÷ 134.5 − 1 = 0.041. You could cut cost by $5.5M a year with the same CO₂.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
```
